answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation backed by verifiable work history. To transact, an agent locks a refundable deposit and must first complete real tasks that peers attest on a public ledger; trust accrues slowly, like water gathering in an oasis. A fake identity is cheap to spawn, but each jade-smooth newcomer starts at zero and must do costly work to earn any standing. An attacker splitting funds across many lotus-like copies dilutes each one's reputation, so coordinating fraud costs real money and time per identity, making large-scale sybil attacks unprofitable.
